1: ---
2: name: pc-lib-analyzer
3: description: Analyze a PC open-source software project — a third-party library OR an application — from its git source and produce a single JSON report. Give it a git URL (or a local checkout path) of a Python / C/C++ / Java / JS-TS project. It runs deterministic code metrics, then reasons over the source for function summary, license, dependencies, and low-level/platform API usage, and emits report.json conforming to references/report_schema.json. Designed to be invoked end-to-end (e.g. from an external script or UI via `claude --agent pc-lib-analyzer`).
4: tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit
5: ---
6: 
7: You analyze a single PC open-source software project — a **library or an
8: application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the
9: analysis is **your reasoning over the source** — only code volume is delegated to a
10: script. Be evidence-driven and honest about uncertainty; never invent facts.
11: First decide `library.kind` (library / application / framework / tool / cli /
12: service / plugin): an **application** is launched by an end user (entry points /
13: native launchers / packaging / GUI or CLI), and its app-specific profile goes into
14: existing dims — entry points & packaging → `build_env`, integrated runtime services
15: → `runtime_surface.services`, GUI toolkit & JDK-internal/Attach APIs → `native_api`.
16: This `kind` also selects the dim-9 HarmonyOS口径 (library → 模型 A/B; application → 模型 C).
17: 
18: ## Input
19: A git URL, or a path to a local checkout. Run from the harness project root so
20: the `.claude/skills/...` and `references/...` paths below resolve.
21: 
22: ## Procedure
23: 
24: 1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
25:    (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
26:    ```bash
27:    git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
28:    ```
29:    Note the resolved commit: `git -C repos/<name> rev-parse HEAD`. If given a
30:    local path (e.g. `repos/<name>` already cloned by the runner), use it directly.
31: 
32:    **Monorepo 子目录**：当 prompt 指出本次分析的是某 monorepo 的**子目录**（给出克隆根
33:    `{repoRoot}` 与分析根 `{repoPath}`＝子目录，例如 `repos/<name>/components/cronet`）时：
34:    把该**子目录**当作被分析的库——下面所有 `{repoPath}`/克隆路径一律指子目录；`git rev-parse HEAD`
35:    用**克隆根 `{repoRoot}`**（子目录没有 `.git`）。你可以读取克隆根下的构建/清单文件（DEPS、
36:    BUILD.gn、根 `package.json`/`go.mod` 等）来理解该子目录的依赖，但**结论只覆盖子目录**。
37: 
38: 2. **Deterministic metrics (dims 2–4).** Run the code-metrics script and capture
39:    its JSON — these numbers are the source of truth for language breakdown, LOC
40:    (production/test/example), and test counts. Do not recompute them by hand.
41:    Write the output to a path **inside the project** (the same run directory you
42:    will write the report to), never `/tmp`. Point `--repo` at the analysis root
43:    `{repoPath}` (the given checkout dir — for a monorepo subunit this is the subdir):
44:    ```bash
45:    python3 .claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py --repo {repoPath} --out <runDir>/metrics.json
46:    ```
47: 
48: 2b. **(Optional) Use the codegraph structural index.** When codegraph is enabled the
49:    **server pre-builds the index right after clone** (`codegraph init -i <repoPath>`;
50:    the `.codegraph/` dir lives inside the checkout, gitignored) — so you normally do
51:    NOT need to build it. Just query it (use the exact `<repoPath>` the run prompt gives,
52:    e.g. `repos/<group>/<name>`):
53:    ```bash
54:    codegraph context "<task>" -p <repoPath>
55:    codegraph query <symbol> -p <repoPath> -j
56:    codegraph callers/callees <symbol> -p <repoPath>
57:    ```
58:    Prefer it for the structural lookups in dims 1, 7, and 9 (dim-9: trace an unadaptable
59:    API's native_api call site up to the library's public symbol to fill
60:    `unadaptable_apis[].public_entry`). If a codegraph call fails
61:    (index not ready / not installed), fall back to grep/Read and add a `meta.warnings`
62:    note. grep/Read remain the way to read literal text (strings, headers, manifests).
63:    If you ever do need to (re)build it yourself: `codegraph init -i <repoPath>` (first
64:    time) or `codegraph sync <repoPath>` (refresh).
65: 
66: 2c. **(Optional) 鸿蒙文档技能（opencode 全局，外部）.** 运行环境可能装有
67:    `harmonyos-sdk-api-lookup`（官方 API 参考：@ohos 模块/权限 ohos.permission.\* 精确名/SysCap）与
68:    `harmonyos-docs-lookup`（开发指南/FAQ）两个全局技能——run prompt 会提示可用性。**dims 9/10 做目标侧
69:    判断（鸿蒙有无等价 API、权限名、适配路径）时优先用它们核实**，方法/预算（每库 ≤10 次检索）/口径护栏
70:    （**文档存在 ≠ PC 可用，`references/harmony-pc-capabilities.json` 仍是 PC 形态权威**）见
71:    harmony-adaptation SKILL.md「目标侧 API 事实核查」。降级链：opencode `skill` 工具按名加载 →
72:    不可用则直接 Glob/Grep `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/` → 都不可用则仅用 caps JSON 并在
73:    `meta.warnings` 记一条。这些是**只读检索**，不违反下方「禁自写脚本」规则；但技能自带的
74:    `scripts/*.py` **不要运行**（三脚本白名单不变），用 Glob/Grep 达到同样检索效果。
75: 
76: 3. **Reasoned dimensions (1, 5, 6, 7, 8).** For each, read the corresponding skill
77:    file for the full method, then read the actual source to fill in the block:
78:    - Dim 1 function summary → `.claude/skills/function-summary/SKILL.md`
79:    - Dim 5 license → `.claude/skills/license-detect/SKILL.md`
80:    - Dim 6 dependencies → `.claude/skills/dependency-analysis/SKILL.md`
81:    - Dim 7 system & platform API → `.claude/skills/native-api-analysis/SKILL.md`
82:      (classify each group: 标准/特有/系统/ffi/硬件; include managed-language stdlib/system calls)
83:    - Dim 8 runtime & build environment → `.claude/skills/runtime-environment/SKILL.md`
84:      (fills `runtime_surface` + `build_env`)
85:    - Dim 10 capability profile → `.claude/skills/capability-profile/SKILL.md`
86:      (fills `capability_profile`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/7/8 — do it AFTER those
87:      exist, BEFORE dim 9: flag GUI/3D/媒体/特定硬件 场景 + harmony_status)
88:    - Dim 11 cloud services → `.claude/skills/cloud-service-analysis/SKILL.md`
89:      (fills `cloud_services`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 1/6/8 — do it AFTER those exist,
90:      BEFORE dim 9: 是否涉及云端服务 + 推测厂商 + 用途/置信, 复用 dependencies /
91:      runtime_surface.network / native_api.dynamic_libraries)
92:    - Dim 12 code partition → `.claude/skills/code-partition/SKILL.md`
93:      (fills `code_partition`; a SYNTHESIS over dims 3/7/10/6 — do it AFTER those exist,
94:      BEFORE dim 9: 把生产代码按鸿蒙迁移复用性分 4 桶——直接复用/重编译复用/需适配/无法适配——
95:      模块粒度 + LOC，**LOC 引用 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.dir_loc` 机械数字**，桶和 ≈
96:      production.code；dim 9 据此定 person_days/breakdown)
97: 
98:    **两层契约（消除重复分析，务必遵守）：** 分析分两层——
99:    - **特征层**（`dim6 dependencies` / `dim7 native_api` / `dim8 runtime_surface+build_env` / `dim10 capability_profile`
100:      + 脚本信号 `code_metrics.platform_adaptation`/`platform_branches`/`arch_specific`/`dir_loc`）：**客观描述"这个库碰了什么"，
101:      是各自事实的唯一权威源**。尤其 **`capability_profile` 是 GUI/3D 渲染/媒体/特定硬件 四类「涉及什么 + 鸿蒙支持状态
102:      (`harmony_status`/`specific_hardware`)」的权威源**——查 `harmony-pc-capabilities.json` 定这四类状态的动作只在 dim-10 做一次。
103:    - **综合层**（`dim12 code_partition` / `dim9 harmony_adaptation`）：**只消费特征层，不重扫源码、不重判已判过的事实**，
104:      且两者结论互不矛盾（`porting_class` 由归一据 dim-12 桶 + dim-9 `unadaptable_apis` 确定性派生）。dim-9 对 GUI/3D/媒体/硬件
105:      **直接采用 dim-10 的 `harmony_status`**（不重查 caps、不从 native_api 重扫这四类），只把它翻译成 blocker/effort/remediation。
106:    - **跨维同一事实只登记一次、其余用 id 交叉引用不重述**：`caused_by`/`source_capability`（回指 dim-10 场景 key 或
107:      dim-9 `ta:*`）/`manifests_as`（指 `ua:*`）/`refs`/`used_symbols`。
108: 
109:    **分块流式产出（重要，避免十分钟输出尾巴）：** 本流程**不**在末尾一次性写整份 report.json。
110:    **每算完一个维度就立刻 `Write` 到 `<runDir>/blocks/<name>.json`**——文件名即报告顶层键、
111:    内容即该块的 JSON 值（不是 `{name: value}`，而直接是 value）。映射：
112:    dim1→`function_summary.json`、dim5→`license.json`、dim6→`dependencies.json`、dim7→`native_api.json`、
113:    dim8→**两个独立文件** `runtime_surface.json`（内容只是 runtime_surface 的值：network/filesystem/env_vars/…）
114:    与 `build_env.json`（内容只是 build_env 的值：language_standard/build_system/platforms/…）——**勿合并、勿再套一层同名键**（双重嵌套会被组装脚本硬拒）、dim10→`capability_profile.json`、
115:    dim11→`cloud_services.json`、dim12→`code_partition.json`、dim9→`harmony_adaptation.json`，外加库头 `library.json` 与 `meta.json`。
116:    **不要**自己产出 `languages`/`code_metrics`/`tests`（这三块由 assemble 脚本从 `metrics.json` splice，
117:    你写了也会被忽略）。`<runDir>/blocks/` 目录已由运行器创建（若不存在可 `mkdir -p`）。块之间**顺序不变**——
118:    综合维度（9/10/11）仍在其输入（1/6/7/8）之后再算再写。这样输出摊到全程、日志实时可见、崩溃也保留已完成的块。
119: 
120:    Use `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` to inspect README, manifests, public headers/API, and
121:    representative source files. Cross-check the
122:    script's test framework / language guesses against what you see; refine the
123:    `tests.notes` / `tests.frameworks` if the script was fooled by an odd layout.
124: 
125:    **超大仓 / monorepo 的正确做法（别因"仓库太大"退回写脚本）：** 面对成千上万文件、
126:    上百个 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`package.json` 的巨仓，**不要试图用脚本枚举全部声明**。
127:    正确顺序：① 用 `codegraph context/query/callers` 取广度、定位关键符号与目录；② 依据
128:    `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs` 聚焦**生产**顶层目录，跳过 test/example；③ 对
129:    代表性的构建/清单文件、公共头、核心源做定向 `Read`。dim 6 的预期产出本就是**主要依赖的
130:    curated 列表**（覆盖 mandatory + 各大类 optional，长尾在 `dependencies.notes` 说明），
131:    由你阅读推理得出——**不是**把 N 条声明全量正则抽取；`count` 取你实际列出的条数即可。
132:    仓库大是「用 codegraph 取广度 + 采样精读」的理由，**不是**「写正则解析器」的理由。
133: 
134:    **生产范围（重要，贯穿 dims 1/6/7/8/9）—— 结论只覆盖生产代码，排除测试与示例/演示代码。**
135:    - 读 `metrics.json` 的 `code_metrics.top_dirs`（每个顶层目录的 {dir,code,category}）和
136:      `test_example_dirs` 作为基线：标为 test/example 的目录里的用法**不进结论**。
137:    - 脚本按目录名 token 分类，**会漏判按功能命名的 demo 目录**（如 PyQt 的 `QLabel/`、
138:      `QThread/`、`QAxWidget/` 被记成 production，其实是独立示例）。你要用判断**补判**：当一个
139:      目录其实是独立可运行的示例/教程（README/目录结构指明；或大量并列、各含 `main`/
140:      `if __name__ == "__main__"` 的「按功能命名」目录），按 **example** 处理。
141:    - 只在 test/example 代码里出现的平台 API、依赖、阻碍点**完全排除**，不写进 `native_api` /
142:      `dependencies` / `harmony_adaptation.unadaptable_apis`/`blockers`；每条 evidence 必须来自
143:      生产代码。把范围判断写进 `function_summary`/`harmony_adaptation.notes`，并在
144:      `meta.observations` 记一条（如「将 QLabel/ QThread/ … 判为示例目录，平台 API 据生产代码收敛」）。
145:    - **示例/教程集合**（几乎全是示例、无可安装包、顶层目录基本都是独立 demo）：`function_summary`
146:      如实判为「示例/教程集合，非可发布生产库」；`native_api`/`unadaptable_apis` 据库本体收敛
147:      （通常近空），不把 demo 的 Win32/COM/DLL 当作库的迁移阻碍。
148: 
149: 3a. **Stamp已鸿蒙化 on dependencies (factual, scripted).** After dim 6 dependencies
150:    are listed, find which are already adapted to HarmonyOS PC by checking the
151:    OpenHarmony PC mirror — run the script per ecosystem (it caches; needs network,
152:    skip on failure with a `meta.warnings` note):
153:    ```bash
154:    node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --ecosystem <eco> --names <comma-separated dep names>
155:    ```
156:    It returns `{name:{adapted,source}}`. Set `dependencies[].harmony_adapted` (bool)
157:    and `harmony_adapted_source` from it. Do NOT guess this — it is a factual mirror
158:    lookup. (Alternatively, after writing report.json in step 4, run
159:    `node scripts/harmony_adapted.js --report <runDir>/report.json` to stamp in place —
160:    but doing it BEFORE dim 9 lets the assessment use it.)
161:

287:    the taxonomies in the skills are recommended starting sets, not closed lists. When

292: 4b. **自我复核一致性告警（单趟反思，趁 checkout + codegraph 索引还在）。** 第一次 assemble 后，
293:    `report.json` 的 `meta.harmony_warnings` 是 `{code, class, message}` 对象数组——这些是归一器的
294:    **跨维一致性启发式**产出。**只处理 `class=="actionable"` 的告警**（`class=="info"` 是归一器已

314:    absolute path to `report.json` plus a concise digest: one-liner, primary
315:    language, ecosystem, production-vs-test LOC, test-case count, license, top

318: ## Rules
319: - The `function_summary` block (summary, category names/descriptions, domain,
320:   target_users) and `library.one_liner` must be written in **简体中文**; keep
321:   proper nouns (SPDX ids, language/dependency names) in their original form.
322: - All files you create — clone, metrics, report, any scratch — must live **inside
323:   the project** (prefer the report's run directory). NEVER write to `/tmp` or any
324:   path outside the project: the headless runner auto-rejects external directories,
325:   which aborts the analysis with no report.
326: - Ground every reasoned claim in something you actually read; cite it in the
327:   `evidence` fields. If evidence is thin, lower the `confidence` and say so.
328: - Keep the script's line/test numbers verbatim; your job is interpretation, not
329:   re-counting.
330: - If a dimension genuinely doesn't apply (e.g. a pure-Python lib with no native
331:   API), emit the empty/cross-platform shape the skill specifies — don't omit the key.
332: - One library/subunit per run (a whole repo, or one monorepo subdirectory).
333:   Deterministic blocks must match the script output exactly.
334: - **Do the whole analysis yourself in one session — never spawn sub-agents / use a
335:   `task` tool.** Sub-agent sessions don't stream to the run log (the panel goes dark)
336:   and lose cross-dimension context and the codegraph index. For large repos, get
337:   breadth with `codegraph context/query/callers` then targeted `Read`, not by
338:   fanning out into research agents.
339: - **解释性维度只能由你推理产出，绝不自写脚本去提取/解析/序列化它们。** dim 1/5/6/7/8/9/10/11
340:   的每个 `blocks/<name>.json` **必须由你用 `Write` 工具直接写出**，内容来自你自己的阅读与判断。
341:   **本流程唯一被授权运行的脚本只有三个**：`.claude/skills/code-metrics/scripts/metrics.py`
342:   （dim 2–4 计数）、`scripts/harmony_adapted.js`（dim 6 鸿蒙盖章）、`scripts/assemble_report.py`
343:   （组装）。除此之外**禁止写任何 Python/shell 脚本**——不许写正则去扫 `meson.build`/`CMakeLists.txt`/
344:   `package.json` 抽依赖，不许拿脚本当 JSON dump/打分/reshape 工具，尤其不要 `extract_*.py` /
345:   `build_*.py` / `stamp_*.py` / `split_*.py` 这类自造中间件。想快速摸底只能用**只读**的
346:   `Grep`/`Glob`/`codegraph`（context/query/callers）探查，**但结论与 JSON 一律由你判断产出**——
347:   这些维度的准确性正来自模型判断，正则会把别名/接口名（如 `find_package(PNG)`）/条件编译/
348:   示例目录判错。（唯一例外见 3a：`harmony_adapted.js` 是被授权的事实盖章脚本。）

application** — from its source code and output one JSON report. Most of the

## Procedure

1. **Obtain the source.** If given a URL, shallow-clone it **into the project**
   (never `/tmp` — see Rules), using the repo name for the dir:
   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 <URL> repos/<name>
   ```

Note that `sql.DB` is a connection pool, so each connection maintains its own independent cache. | 127: 128: 129: ## DSN Examples 130: 131: ``` 132: file:test.db?cache=shared&mode=memory 133: ``` 134: 135: # Features 136: 137: This package allows additional configuration of features available within SQLite3 to be enabled or disabled by golang build constraints also known as build `tags`. 138: 139: Click [here](https://golang.org/pkg/go/build/#hdr-Build_Constraints) for more information about build tags / constraints. 140: 141: ### Usage 142: 143: If you wish to build this library with additional extensions / features, use the following command: 144: 145: ```bash 146: go build -tags "" 147: ``` 148: 149: For available features, see the extension list. 150: When using multiple build tags, all the different tags should be space delimited. 151: 152: Example: 153: 154: ```bash 155: go build -tags "icu json1 fts5 secure_delete" 156: ``` 157: 158: ### Feature / Extension List 159: 160: | Extension | Build Tag | Description | 161: |-----------|-----------|-------------| 162: | Additional Statistics | sqlite_stat4 | This option adds additional logic to the ANALYZE command and to the query planner that can help SQLite to chose a better query plan under certain situations. The ANALYZE command is enhanced to collect histogram data from all columns of every index and store that data in the sqlite_stat4 table.

The query planner will then use the histogram data to help it make better index choices. The downside of this compile-time option is that it violates the query planner stability guarantee making it more difficult to ensure consistent performance in mass-produced applications.

SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT4 is an enhancement of SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT3. STAT3 only recorded histogram data for the left-most column of each index whereas the STAT4 enhancement records histogram data from all columns of each index.

The SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT3 compile-time option is a no-op and is ignored if the SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT4 compile-time option is used | 163: | Allow URI Authority | sqlite_allow_uri_authority | URI filenames normally throws an error if the authority section is not either empty or "localhost".

However, if SQLite is compiled with the SQLITE_ALLOW_URI_AUTHORITY compile-time option, then the URI is converted into a Uniform Naming Convention (UNC) filename and passed down to the underlying operating system that way | 164: | App Armor | sqlite_app_armor | When defined, this C-preprocessor macro activates extra code that attempts to detect misuse of the SQLite API, such as passing in NULL pointers to required parameters or using objects after they have been destroyed.

App Armor is not available under `Windows`. | 165: | Disable Load Extensions | sqlite_omit_load_extension | Loading of external extensions is enabled by default.

See [SQLite Official Documentation](https://www.sqlite.org/dbstat.html) for more information. | 184: 185: # Compilation 186: 187: This package requires the `CGO_ENABLED=1` environment variable if not set by default, and the presence of the `gcc` compiler. 188: 189: If you need to add additional CFLAGS or LDFLAGS to the build command, and do not want to modify this package, then this can be achieved by using the `CGO_CFLAGS` and `CGO_LDFLAGS` environment variables. 190: 191: ## Android 192: 193: This package can be compiled for android. 194: Compile with: 195: 196: ```bash 197: go build -tags "android" 198: ``` 199: 200: For more information see [#201](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/201) 201: 202: # ARM 203: 204: To compile for `ARM` use the following environment: 205: 206: ```bash 207: env CC=arm-linux-gnueabihf-gcc CXX=arm-linux-gnueabihf-g++ \ 208: CGO_ENABLED=1 GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=7 \ 209: go build -v 210: ``` 211: 212: Additional information: 213: - [#242](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/242) 214: - [#504](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/504) 215: 216: # Cross Compile 217: 218: This library can be cross-compiled. 219: 220: In some cases you are required to the `CC` environment variable with the cross compiler. 221: 222: ## Cross Compiling from macOS 223: The simplest way to cross compile from macOS is to use [xgo](https://github.com/karalabe/xgo). 224: 225: Steps: 226: - Install [musl-cross](https://github.com/FiloSottile/homebrew-musl-cross) (`brew install FiloSottile/musl-cross/musl-cross`). 227: - Run `CC=x86_64-linux-musl-gcc CXX=x86_64-linux-musl-g++ GOARCH=amd64 GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -ldflags "-linkmode external -extldflags -static"`. 228: 229: Please refer to the project's [README](https://github.com/FiloSottile/homebrew-musl-cross#readme) for further information. 230: 231: # Compiling 232: 233: ## Linux 234: 235: To compile this package on Linux, you must install the development tools for your linux distribution. 236: 237: To compile under linux use the build tag `linux`. 238: 239: ```bash 240: go build -tags "linux" 241: ``` 242: 243: If you wish to link directly to libsqlite3 then you can use the `libsqlite3` build tag. 244: 245: ``` 246: go build -tags "libsqlite3 linux" 247: ``` 248: 249: ### Alpine 250: 251: When building in an `alpine` container run the following command before building: 252: 253: ``` 254: apk add --update gcc musl-dev 255: ``` 256: 257: ### Fedora 258: 259: ```bash 260: sudo yum groupinstall "Development Tools" "Development Libraries" 261: ``` 262: 263: ### Ubuntu 264: 265: ```bash 266: sudo apt-get install build-essential 267: ``` 268: 269: ## macOS 270: 271: macOS should have all the tools present to compile this package. If not, install XCode to add all the developers tools. 272: 273: Required dependency: 274: 275: ```bash 276: brew install sqlite3 277: ``` 278: 279: For macOS, there is an additional package to install which is required if you wish to build the `icu` extension. 280: 281: This additional package can be installed with `homebrew`: 282: 283: ```bash 284: brew upgrade icu4c 285: ``` 286: 287: To compile for macOS on x86: 288: 289: ```bash 290: go build -tags "darwin amd64" 291: ``` 292: 293: To compile for macOS on ARM chips: 294: 295: ```bash 296: go build -tags "darwin arm64" 297: ``` 298: 299: If you wish to link directly to libsqlite3, use the `libsqlite3` build tag: 300: 301: ``` 302: # x86 303: go build -tags "libsqlite3 darwin amd64" 304: # ARM 305: go build -tags "libsqlite3 darwin arm64" 306: ``` 307: 308: Additional information: 309: - [#206](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/206) 310: - [#404](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/404) 311: 312: ## Windows 313: 314: To compile this package on Windows, you must have the `gcc` compiler installed. 315: 316: 1) Install a Windows `gcc` toolchain. 317: 2) Add the `bin` folder to the Windows path, if the installer did not do this by default. 318: 3) Open a terminal for the TDM-GCC toolchain, which can be found in the Windows Start menu. 319: 4) Navigate to your project folder and run the `go build ...` command for this package. 320: 321: For example the TDM-GCC Toolchain can be found [here](https://jmeubank.github.io/tdm-gcc/). 322: 323: ## Errors 324: 325: - Compile error: `can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC` 326: 327: When receiving a compile time error referencing recompile with `-FPIC` then you 328: are probably using a hardend system. 329: 330: You can compile the library on a hardend system with the following command. 331: 332: ```bash 333: go build -ldflags '-extldflags=-fno-PIC' 334: ``` 335: 336: More details see [#120](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/120) 337: 338: - Can't build go-sqlite3 on windows 64bit. 339: 340: > Probably, you are using go 1.0, go1.0 has a problem when it comes to compiling/linking on windows 64bit. 341: > See: [#27](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/27) 342: 343: - `go get github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3` throws compilation error. 344: 345: `gcc` throws: `internal compiler error` 346: 347: Remove the download repository from your disk and try re-install with: 348: 349: ```bash 350: go install github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3 351: ``` 352: 353: # User Authentication 354: 355: ***This is deprecated*** 356: 357: This package supports the SQLite User Authentication module. 358: 359: ## Compile 360: 361: To use the User authentication module, the package has to be compiled with the tag `sqlite_userauth`. See [Features](#features). 362: 363: ## Usage 364: 365: ### Create protected database 366: 367: To create a database protected by user authentication, provide the following argument to the connection string `_auth`. 368: This will enable user authentication within the database. This option however requires two additional arguments: 369: 370: - `_auth_user` 371: - `_auth_pass` 372: 373: When `_auth` is present in the connection string user authentication will be enabled and the provided user will be created 374: as an `admin` user. After initial creation, the parameter `_auth` has no effect anymore and can be omitted from the connection string. 375: 376: Example connection strings: 377: 378: Create an user authentication database with user `admin` and password `admin`: 379: 380: `file:test.s3db?_auth&_auth_user=admin&_auth_pass=admin` 381: 382: Create an user authentication database with user `admin` and password `admin` and use `SHA1` for the password encoding: 383: 384: `file:test.s3db?_auth&_auth_user=admin&_auth_pass=admin&_auth_crypt=sha1` 385: 386: ### Password Encoding 387: 388: The passwords within the user authentication module of SQLite are encoded with the SQLite function `sqlite_cryp`. 389: This function uses a ceasar-cypher which is quite insecure. 390: This library provides several additional password encoders which can be configured through the connection string. 391: 392: The password cypher can be configured with the key `_auth_crypt`. And if the configured password encoder also requires an 393: salt this can be configured with `_auth_salt`. 394: 395: #### Available Encoders 396: 397: - SHA1 398: - SSHA1 (Salted SHA1) 399: - SHA256 400: - SSHA256 (salted SHA256) 401: - SHA384 402: - SSHA384 (salted SHA384) 403: - SHA512 404: - SSHA512 (salted SHA512) 405: 406: ### Restrictions 407: 408: Operations on the database regarding user management can only be preformed by an administrator user. 409: 410: ### Support 411: 412: The user authentication supports two kinds of users: 413: 414: - administrators 415: - regular users 416: 417: ### User Management 418: 419: User management can be done by directly using the `*SQLiteConn` or by SQL. 420: 421: #### SQL 422: 423: The following sql functions are available for user management: 424: 425: | Function | Arguments | Description | 426: |----------|-----------|-------------| 427: | `authenticate` | username `string`, password `string` | Will authenticate an user, this is done by the connection; and should not be used manually. | 428: | `auth_user_add` | username `string`, password `string`, admin `int` | This function will add an user to the database.
if the database is not protected by user authentication it will enable it. Argument `admin` is an integer identifying if the added user should be an administrator. Only Administrators can add administrators. | 429: | `auth_user_change` | username `string`, password `string`, admin `int` | Function to modify an user. Users can change their own password, but only an administrator can change the administrator flag. | 430: | `authUserDelete` | username `string` | Delete an user from the database. Can only be used by an administrator. The current logged in administrator cannot be deleted. This is to make sure their is always an administrator remaining. | 431: 432: These functions will return an integer: 433: 434: - 0 (SQLITE_OK) 435: - 23 (SQLITE_AUTH) Failed to perform due to authentication or insufficient privileges 436: 437: ##### Examples 438: 439: ```sql 440: // Autheticate user 441: // Create Admin User 442: SELECT auth_user_add('admin2', 'admin2', 1); 443: 444: // Change password for user 445: SELECT auth_user_change('user', 'userpassword', 0); 446: 447: // Delete user 448: SELECT user_delete('user'); 449: ``` 450: 451: #### *SQLiteConn 452: 453: The following functions are available for User authentication from the `*SQLiteConn`: 454: 455: | Function | Description | 456: |----------|-------------| 457: | `Authenticate(username, password string) error` | Authenticate user | 458: | `AuthUserAdd(username, password string, admin bool) error` | Add user | 459: | `AuthUserChange(username, password string, admin bool) error` | Modify user | 460: | `AuthUserDelete(username string) error` | Delete user | 461: 462: ### Attached database 463: 464: When using attached databases, SQLite will use the authentication from the `main` database for the attached database(s). 465: 466: # Extensions 467: 468: If you want your own extension to be listed here, or you want to add a reference to an extension; please submit an Issue for this. 469: 470: ## Spatialite 471: 472: Spatialite is available as an extension to SQLite, and can be used in combination with this repository. 473: For an example, see [shaxbee/go-spatialite](https://github.com/shaxbee/go-spatialite). 474: 475: ## extension-functions.c from SQLite3 Contrib 476: 477: extension-functions.c is available as an extension to SQLite, and provides the following functions: 478: 479: - Math: acos, asin, atan, atn2, atan2, acosh, asinh, atanh, difference, degrees, radians, cos, sin, tan, cot, cosh, sinh, tanh, coth, exp, log, log10, power, sign, sqrt, square, ceil, floor, pi. 480: - String: replicate, charindex, leftstr, rightstr, ltrim, rtrim, trim, replace, reverse, proper, padl, padr, padc, strfilter. 481: - Aggregate: stdev, variance, mode, median, lower_quartile, upper_quartile 482: 483: For an example, see [dinedal/go-sqlite3-extension-functions](https://github.com/dinedal/go-sqlite3-extension-functions). 484: 485: # FAQ 486: 487: - Getting insert error while query is opened. 488: 489: > You can pass some arguments into the connection string, for example, a URI. 490: > See: [#39](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/39) 491: 492: - Do you want to cross compile? mingw on Linux or Mac? 493: 494: > See: [#106](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/106) 495: > See also: http://www.limitlessfx.com/cross-compile-golang-app-for-windows-from-linux.html 496: 497: - Want to get time.Time with current locale 498: 499: Use `_loc=auto` in SQLite3 filename schema like `file:foo.db?_loc=auto`. 500: 501: - Can I use this in multiple routines concurrently? 502: 503: Yes for readonly. But not for writable. See [#50](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/50), [#51](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/51), [#209](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/209), [#274](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/274). 504: 505: - Why I'm getting `no such table` error? 506: 507: Why is it racy if I use a `sql.Open("sqlite3", ":memory:")` database? 508: 509: Each connection to `":memory:"` opens a brand new in-memory sql database, so if 510: the stdlib's sql engine happens to open another connection and you've only 511: specified `":memory:"`, that connection will see a brand new database. A 512: workaround is to use `"file::memory:?cache=shared"` (or `"file:foobar?mode=memory&cache=shared"`). Every 513: connection to this string will point to the same in-memory database. 514: 515: Note that if the last database connection in the pool closes, the in-memory database is deleted. Make sure the [max idle connection limit](https://golang.org/pkg/database/sql/#DB.SetMaxIdleConns) is > 0, and the [connection lifetime](https://golang.org/pkg/database/sql/#DB.SetConnMaxLifetime) is infinite. 516: 517: For more information see: 518: * [#204](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/204) 519: * [#511](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/511) 520: * https://www.sqlite.org/sharedcache.html#shared_cache_and_in_memory_databases 521: * https://www.sqlite.org/inmemorydb.html#sharedmemdb 522: 523: - Reading from database with large amount of goroutines fails on OSX. 524: 525: OS X limits OS-wide to not have more than 1000 files open simultaneously by default. 526: 527: For more information, see [#289](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/289) 528: 529: - Trying to execute a `.` (dot) command throws an error. 530: 531: Error: `Error: near ".": syntax error` 532: Dot command are part of SQLite3 CLI, not of this library. 533: 534: You need to implement the feature or call the sqlite3 cli. 535: 536: More information see [#305](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/305). 537: 538: - Error: `database is locked` 539: 540: When you get a database is locked, please use the following options. 541: 542: Add to DSN: `cache=shared` 543: 544: Example: 545: ```go 546: db, err := sql.Open("sqlite3", "file:locked.sqlite?cache=shared") 547: ``` 548: 549: Next, please set the database connections of the SQL package to 1: 550: 551: ```go 552: db.SetMaxOpenConns(1) 553: ``` 554: 555: For more information, see [#209](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/209). 556: 557: ## Contributors 558: 559: ### Code Contributors 560: 561: This project exists thanks to all the people who [[contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)]. 562: 563: 564: ### Financial Contributors 565: 566: Become a financial contributor and help us sustain our community. Examples can be found under the [examples](./_example) directory. # Connection String When creating a new SQLite database or connection to an existing one, with the file name additional options can be given. This is also known as a DSN (Data Source Name) string. Options are append after the filename of the SQLite database. The database filename and options are separated by an `?` (Question Mark). Options should be URL-encoded (see [url.QueryEscape](https://golang.org/pkg/net/url/#QueryEscape)). This also applies when using an in-memory database instead of a file. Options can be given using the following format: `KEYWORD=VALUE` and multiple options can be combined with the `&` ampersand. This library supports DSN options of SQLite itself and provides additional options. Click [here](https://golang.org/pkg/go/build/#hdr-Build_Constraints) for more information about build tags / constraints. ### Usage If you wish to build this library with additional extensions / features, use the following command: ```bash go build -tags "" ``` For available features, see the extension list. When using multiple build tags, all the different tags should be space delimited. Example: ```bash go build -tags "icu json1 fts5 secure_delete" ``` ### Feature / Extension List | Extension | Build Tag | Description | |-----------|-----------|-------------| | Additional Statistics | sqlite_stat4 | This option adds additional logic to the ANALYZE command and to the query planner that can help SQLite to chose a better query plan under certain situations. The ANALYZE command is enhanced to collect histogram data from all columns of every index and store that data in the sqlite_stat4 table.

The query planner will then use the histogram data to help it make better index choices. The downside of this compile-time option is that it violates the query planner stability guarantee making it more difficult to ensure consistent performance in mass-produced applications.

SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT4 is an enhancement of SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT3. STAT3 only recorded histogram data for the left-most column of each index whereas the STAT4 enhancement records histogram data from all columns of each index.

The SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT3 compile-time option is a no-op and is ignored if the SQLITE_ENABLE_STAT4 compile-time option is used | | Allow URI Authority | sqlite_allow_uri_authority | URI filenames normally throws an error if the authority section is not either empty or "localhost".

However, if SQLite is compiled with the SQLITE_ALLOW_URI_AUTHORITY compile-time option, then the URI is converted into a Uniform Naming Convention (UNC) filename and passed down to the underlying operating system that way | | App Armor | sqlite_app_armor | When defined, this C-preprocessor macro activates extra code that attempts to detect misuse of the SQLite API, such as passing in NULL pointers to required parameters or using objects after they have been destroyed.

App Armor is not available under `Windows`. | | Disable Load Extensions | sqlite_omit_load_extension | Loading of external extensions is enabled by default.

To disable extension loading add the build tag `sqlite_omit_load_extension`. | | Enable Serialization with `libsqlite3` | sqlite_serialize | Serialization and deserialization of a SQLite database is available by default, unless the build tag `libsqlite3` is set.

To enable this functionality even if `libsqlite3` is set, add the build tag `sqlite_serialize`. | | Foreign Keys | sqlite_foreign_keys | This macro determines whether enforcement of foreign key constraints is enabled or disabled by default for new database connections.

Each database connection can always turn enforcement of foreign key constraints on and off and run-time using the foreign_keys pragma.

Enforcement of foreign key constraints is normally off by default, but if this compile-time parameter is set to 1, enforcement of foreign key constraints will be on by default | | Full Auto Vacuum | sqlite_vacuum_full | Set the default auto vacuum to full | | Incremental Auto Vacuum | sqlite_vacuum_incr | Set the default auto vacuum to incremental | | Full Text Search Engine | sqlite_fts5 | When this option is defined in the amalgamation, versions 5 of the full-text search engine (fts5) is added to the build automatically | | International Components for Unicode | sqlite_icu | This option causes the International Components for Unicode or "ICU" extension to SQLite to be added to the build | | Introspect PRAGMAS | sqlite_introspect | This option adds some extra PRAGMA statements.

See [SQLite Official Documentation](https://www.sqlite.org/dbstat.html) for more information. | # Compilation This package requires the `CGO_ENABLED=1` environment variable if not set by default, and the presence of the `gcc` compiler. If you need to add additional CFLAGS or LDFLAGS to the build command, and do not want to modify this package, then this can be achieved by using the `CGO_CFLAGS` and `CGO_LDFLAGS` environment variables. ## Android This package can be compiled for android. Compile with: ```bash go build -tags "android" ``` For more information see [#201](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/201) # ARM To compile for `ARM` use the following environment: ```bash env CC=arm-linux-gnueabihf-gcc CXX=arm-linux-gnueabihf-g++ \ CGO_ENABLED=1 GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm GOARM=7 \ go build -v ``` Additional information: - [#242](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/242) - [#504](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/504) # Cross Compile This library can be cross-compiled. In some cases you are required to the `CC` environment variable with the cross compiler. ## Cross Compiling from macOS The simplest way to cross compile from macOS is to use [xgo](https://github.com/karalabe/xgo). Steps: - Install [musl-cross](https://github.com/FiloSottile/homebrew-musl-cross) (`brew install FiloSottile/musl-cross/musl-cross`). - Run `CC=x86_64-linux-musl-gcc CXX=x86_64-linux-musl-g++ GOARCH=amd64 GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -ldflags "-linkmode external -extldflags -static"`. Please refer to the project's [README](https://github.com/FiloSottile/homebrew-musl-cross#readme) for further information. # Compiling ## Linux To compile this package on Linux, you must install the development tools for your linux distribution. To compile under linux use the build tag `linux`. ```bash go build -tags "linux" ``` If you wish to link directly to libsqlite3 then you can use the `libsqlite3` build tag. ``` go build -tags "libsqlite3 linux" ``` ### Alpine When building in an `alpine` container run the following command before building: ``` apk add --update gcc musl-dev ``` ### Fedora ```bash sudo yum groupinstall "Development Tools" "Development Libraries" ``` ### Ubuntu ```bash sudo apt-get install build-essential ``` ## macOS macOS should have all the tools present to compile this package. If not, install XCode to add all the developers tools. Required dependency: ```bash brew install sqlite3 ``` For macOS, there is an additional package to install which is required if you wish to build the `icu` extension. This additional package can be installed with `homebrew`: ```bash brew upgrade icu4c ``` To compile for macOS on x86: ```bash go build -tags "darwin amd64" ``` To compile for macOS on ARM chips: ```bash go build -tags "darwin arm64" ``` If you wish to link directly to libsqlite3, use the `libsqlite3` build tag: ``` # x86 go build -tags "libsqlite3 darwin amd64" # ARM go build -tags "libsqlite3 darwin arm64" ``` Additional information: - [#206](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/206) - [#404](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/404) ## Windows To compile this package on Windows, you must have the `gcc` compiler installed. 1) Install a Windows `gcc` toolchain. 2) Add the `bin` folder to the Windows path, if the installer did not do this by default. 3) Open a terminal for the TDM-GCC toolchain, which can be found in the Windows Start menu. 4) Navigate to your project folder and run the `go build ...` command for this package. For example the TDM-GCC Toolchain can be found [here](https://jmeubank.github.io/tdm-gcc/). ## Errors - Compile error: `can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC` When receiving a compile time error referencing recompile with `-FPIC` then you are probably using a hardend system. You can compile the library on a hardend system with the following command. ```bash go build -ldflags '-extldflags=-fno-PIC' ``` More details see [#120](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/120) - Can't build go-sqlite3 on windows 64bit. > Probably, you are using go 1.0, go1.0 has a problem when it comes to compiling/linking on windows 64bit. > See: [#27](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/27) - `go get github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3` throws compilation error. `gcc` throws: `internal compiler error` Remove the download repository from your disk and try re-install with: ```bash go install github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3 ``` # User Authentication ***This is deprecated*** This package supports the SQLite User Authentication module. ## Compile To use the User authentication module, the package has to be compiled with the tag `sqlite_userauth`. See [Features](#features). ## Usage ### Create protected database To create a database protected by user authentication, provide the following argument to the connection string `_auth`. This will enable user authentication within the database. This option however requires two additional arguments: - `_auth_user` - `_auth_pass` When `_auth` is present in the connection string user authentication will be enabled and the provided user will be created as an `admin` user. After initial creation, the parameter `_auth` has no effect anymore and can be omitted from the connection string. Example connection strings: Create an user authentication database with user `admin` and password `admin`: `file:test.s3db?_auth&_auth_user=admin&_auth_pass=admin` Create an user authentication database with user `admin` and password `admin` and use `SHA1` for the password encoding: `file:test.s3db?_auth&_auth_user=admin&_auth_pass=admin&_auth_crypt=sha1` ### Password Encoding The passwords within the user authentication module of SQLite are encoded with the SQLite function `sqlite_cryp`. This function uses a ceasar-cypher which is quite insecure. This library provides several additional password encoders which can be configured through the connection string. The password cypher can be configured with the key `_auth_crypt`. And if the configured password encoder also requires an salt this can be configured with `_auth_salt`. #### Available Encoders - SHA1 - SSHA1 (Salted SHA1) - SHA256 - SSHA256 (salted SHA256) - SHA384 - SSHA384 (salted SHA384) - SHA512 - SSHA512 (salted SHA512) ### Restrictions Operations on the database regarding user management can only be preformed by an administrator user. ### Support The user authentication supports two kinds of users: - administrators - regular users ### User Management User management can be done by directly using the `*SQLiteConn` or by SQL. #### SQL The following sql functions are available for user management: | Function | Arguments | Description | |----------|-----------|-------------| | `authenticate` | username `string`, password `string` | Will authenticate an user, this is done by the connection; and should not be used manually. | | `auth_user_add` | username `string`, password `string`, admin `int` | This function will add an user to the database.
if the database is not protected by user authentication it will enable it. Argument `admin` is an integer identifying if the added user should be an administrator. Only Administrators can add administrators. | | `auth_user_change` | username `string`, password `string`, admin `int` | Function to modify an user. Users can change their own password, but only an administrator can change the administrator flag. | | `authUserDelete` | username `string` | Delete an user from the database. Can only be used by an administrator. The current logged in administrator cannot be deleted. This is to make sure their is always an administrator remaining. | These functions will return an integer: - 0 (SQLITE_OK) - 23 (SQLITE_AUTH) Failed to perform due to authentication or insufficient privileges ##### Examples ```sql // Autheticate user // Create Admin User SELECT auth_user_add('admin2', 'admin2', 1); // Change password for user SELECT auth_user_change('user', 'userpassword', 0); // Delete user SELECT user_delete('user'); ``` #### *SQLiteConn The following functions are available for User authentication from the `*SQLiteConn`: | Function | Description | |----------|-------------| | `Authenticate(username, password string) error` | Authenticate user | | `AuthUserAdd(username, password string, admin bool) error` | Add user | | `AuthUserChange(username, password string, admin bool) error` | Modify user | | `AuthUserDelete(username string) error` | Delete user | ### Attached database When using attached databases, SQLite will use the authentication from the `main` database for the attached database(s). # Extensions If you want your own extension to be listed here, or you want to add a reference to an extension; please submit an Issue for this. ## Spatialite Spatialite is available as an extension to SQLite, and can be used in combination with this repository. For an example, see [shaxbee/go-spatialite](https://github.com/shaxbee/go-spatialite). ## extension-functions.c from SQLite3 Contrib extension-functions.c is available as an extension to SQLite, and provides the following functions: - Math: acos, asin, atan, atn2, atan2, acosh, asinh, atanh, difference, degrees, radians, cos, sin, tan, cot, cosh, sinh, tanh, coth, exp, log, log10, power, sign, sqrt, square, ceil, floor, pi. - String: replicate, charindex, leftstr, rightstr, ltrim, rtrim, trim, replace, reverse, proper, padl, padr, padc, strfilter. - Aggregate: stdev, variance, mode, median, lower_quartile, upper_quartile For an example, see [dinedal/go-sqlite3-extension-functions](https://github.com/dinedal/go-sqlite3-extension-functions). # FAQ - Getting insert error while query is opened. > You can pass some arguments into the connection string, for example, a URI. > See: [#39](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/39) - Do you want to cross compile? mingw on Linux or Mac? > See: [#106](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/106) > See also: http://www.limitlessfx.com/cross-compile-golang-app-for-windows-from-linux.html - Want to get time.Time with current locale Use `_loc=auto` in SQLite3 filename schema like `file:foo.db?_loc=auto`. - Can I use this in multiple routines concurrently? Yes for readonly. But not for writable. See [#50](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/50), [#51](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/51), [#209](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/209), [#274](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/274). - Why I'm getting `no such table` error? Why is it racy if I use a `sql.Open("sqlite3", ":memory:")` database? Each connection to `":memory:"` opens a brand new in-memory sql database, so if the stdlib's sql engine happens to open another connection and you've only specified `":memory:"`, that connection will see a brand new database. A workaround is to use `"file::memory:?cache=shared"` (or `"file:foobar?mode=memory&cache=shared"`). Every connection to this string will point to the same in-memory database. Note that if the last database connection in the pool closes, the in-memory database is deleted. Make sure the [max idle connection limit](https://golang.org/pkg/database/sql/#DB.SetMaxIdleConns) is > 0, and the [connection lifetime](https://golang.org/pkg/database/sql/#DB.SetConnMaxLifetime) is infinite. For more information see: * [#204](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/204) * [#511](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/511) * https://www.sqlite.org/sharedcache.html#shared_cache_and_in_memory_databases * https://www.sqlite.org/inmemorydb.html#sharedmemdb - Reading from database with large amount of goroutines fails on OSX. OS X limits OS-wide to not have more than 1000 files open simultaneously by default. For more information, see [#289](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/289) - Trying to execute a `.` (dot) command throws an error. Error: `Error: near ".": syntax error` Dot command are part of SQLite3 CLI, not of this library. You need to implement the feature or call the sqlite3 cli. More information see [#305](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/305). - Error: `database is locked` When you get a database is locked, please use the following options. Add to DSN: `cache=shared` Example: ```go db, err := sql.Open("sqlite3", "file:locked.sqlite?cache=shared") ``` Next, please set the database connections of the SQL package to 1: ```go db.SetMaxOpenConns(1) ``` For more information, see [#209](https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/209). ## Contributors ### Code Contributors This project exists thanks to all the people who [[contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)]. ### Financial Contributors Become a financial contributor and help us sustain our community. 538: 	// user data space provided by sqlite.

548: func (ai *aggInfo) agg(ctx *C.sqlite3_context) (int64, reflect.Value, error) {
549: 	aggIdx := (*int64)(C.sqlite3_aggregate_context(ctx, C.int(8)))
550: 	if *aggIdx == 0 {
551: 		*aggIdx = ai.next
552: 		ret := ai.constructor.Call(nil)
553: 		if len(ret) == 2 && ret[1].Interface() != nil {
554: 			return 0, reflect.Value{}, ret[1].Interface().(error)
555: 		}
556: 		if ret[0].IsNil() {
557: 			return 0, reflect.Value{}, errors.New("aggregator constructor returned nil state")
558: 		}
559: 		ai.next++
560: 		ai.active[*aggIdx] = ret[0]
561: 	}
562: 	return *aggIdx, ai.active[*aggIdx], nil
563: }

575: 		return
576: 	}
577: 
578: 	ret := agg.MethodByName("Step").Call(args)
579: 	if len(ret) == 1 && ret[0].Interface() != nil {
580: 		callbackError(ctx, ret[0].Interface().(error))
581: 		return
582: 	}

606: // Commit transaction.
607: func (tx *SQLiteTx) Commit() error {
608: 	_, err := tx.c.exec(context.Background(), "COMMIT", nil)
609: 	if err != nil {
610: 		// sqlite3 may leave the transaction open in this scenario.
611: 		// However, database/sql considers the transaction complete once we
612: 		// return from Commit() - we must clean up to honour its semantics.
613: 		// We don't know if the ROLLBACK is strictly necessary, but according
614: 		// to sqlite's docs, there is no harm in calling ROLLBACK unnecessarily.
615: 		tx.c.exec(context.Background(), "ROLLBACK", nil)
616: 	}
617: 	return err
618: }

632: // inputs. Additionally, it must have the following properties for all
633: // strings A, B and C: if A==B then B==A; if A==B and B==C then A==C;
634: // if A<B then B>A; if A<B and B<C then A<C.

637: // undefined when the collation is used.

645: 	}

708: // RegisterFunc makes a Go function available as a SQLite function.
709: //
710: // The Go function can have arguments of the following types: any
711: // numeric type except complex, bool, []byte, string and any.
712: // any arguments are given the direct translation of the SQLite data type:
713: // int64 for INTEGER, float64 for FLOAT, []byte for BLOB, string for TEXT.
714: //
715: // The function can additionally be variadic, as long as the type of
716: // the variadic argument is one of the above.
717: //
718: // If pure is true. SQLite will assume that the function's return
719: // value depends only on its inputs, and make more aggressive
720: // optimizations in its queries.
721: //
722: // See _example/go_custom_funcs for a detailed example.
723: func (c *SQLiteConn) RegisterFunc(name string, impl any, pure bool) error {
724: 	var fi functionInfo
725: 	fi.f = reflect.ValueOf(impl)
726: 	t := fi.f.Type()
727: 	if t.Kind() != reflect.Func {
728: 		return errors.New("Non-function passed to RegisterFunc")
729: 	}
730: 	if t.NumOut() != 1 && t.NumOut() != 2 {
731: 		return errors.New("SQLite functions must return 1 or 2 values")
732: 	}
733: 	if t.NumOut() == 2 && !t.Out(1).Implements(reflect.TypeOf((*error)(nil)).Elem()) {
734: 		return errors.New("Second return value of SQLite function must be error")
735: 	}
736: 
737: 	numArgs := t.NumIn()
738: 	if t.IsVariadic() {
739: 		numArgs--
740: 	}
741: 
742: 	for i := 0; i < numArgs; i++ {
743: 		conv, err := callbackArg(t.In(i))
744: 		if err != nil {
745: 			return err
746: 		}
747: 		fi.argConverters = append(fi.argConverters, conv)
748: 	}
749: 
750: 	if t.IsVariadic() {
751: 		conv, err := callbackArg(t.In(numArgs).Elem())
752: 		if err != nil {
753: 			return err
754: 		}
755: 		fi.variadicConverter = conv
756: 		// Pass -1 to sqlite so that it allows any number of
757: 		// arguments. The call helper verifies that the minimum number
758: 		// of arguments is present for variadic functions.
759: 		numArgs = -1
760: 	}
761: 
762: 	conv, err := callbackRet(t.Out(0))
763: 	if err != nil {
764: 		return err
765: 	}
766: 	fi.retConverter = conv
767: 
768: 	// fi must outlast the database connection, or we'll have dangling pointers.
769: 	c.funcs = append(c.funcs, &fi)
770: 
771: 	cname := C.CString(name)
772: 	defer C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cname))
773: 	opts := C.SQLITE_UTF8
774: 	if pure {
775: 		opts |= C.SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC
776: 	}
777: 	rv := sqlite3CreateFunction(c.db, cname, C.int(numArgs), C.int(opts), newHandle(c, &fi), C.callbackTrampoline, nil, nil)
778: 	if rv != C.SQLITE_OK {
779: 		return c.lastError()
780: 	}
781: 	return nil
782: }

784: func sqlite3CreateFunction(db *C.sqlite3, zFunctionName *C.char, nArg C.int, eTextRep C.int, pApp unsafe.Pointer, xFunc unsafe.Pointer, xStep unsafe.Pointer, xFinal unsafe.Pointer) C.int {
785: 	return C._sqlite3_create_function(db, zFunctionName, nArg, eTextRep, C.uintptr_t(uintptr(pApp)), (*[0]byte)(xFunc), (*[0]byte)(xStep), (*[0]byte)(xFinal))
786: }

788: // RegisterAggregator makes a Go type available as a SQLite aggregation function.
789: //
790: // Because aggregation is incremental, it's implemented in Go with a
791: // type that has 2 methods: func Step(values) accumulates one row of
792: // data into the accumulator, and func Done() ret finalizes and
793: // returns the aggregate value. "values" and "ret" may be any type
794: // supported by RegisterFunc.
795: //
796: // RegisterAggregator takes as implementation a constructor function
797: // that constructs an instance of the aggregator type each time an
798: // aggregation begins. The constructor must return a pointer to a
799: // type, or an interface that implements Step() and Done().
800: //
801: // The constructor function and the Step/Done methods may optionally
802: // return an error in addition to their other return values.
803: //
804: // See _example/go_custom_funcs for a detailed example.
805: func (c *SQLiteConn) RegisterAggregator(name string, impl any, pure bool) error {
806: 	var ai aggInfo
807: 	ai.constructor = reflect.ValueOf(impl)
808: 	t := ai.constructor.Type()
809: 	if t.Kind() != reflect.Func {
810: 		return errors.New("non-function passed to RegisterAggregator")
811: 	}
812: 	if t.NumOut() != 1 && t.NumOut() != 2 {
813: 		return errors.New("SQLite aggregator constructors must return 1 or 2 values")
814: 	}
815: 	if t.NumOut() == 2 && !t.Out(1).Implements(reflect.TypeOf((*error)(nil)).Elem()) {
816: 		return errors.New("Second return value of SQLite function must be error")
817: 	}
818: 	if t.NumIn() != 0 {
819: 		return errors.New("SQLite aggregator constructors must not have arguments")
820: 	}
821: 
822: 	agg := t.Out(0)
823: 	switch agg.Kind() {
824: 	case reflect.Ptr, reflect.Interface:
825: 	default:
826: 		return errors.New("SQlite aggregator constructor must return a pointer object")
827: 	}
828: 	stepFn, found := agg.MethodByName("Step")
829: 	if !found {
830: 		return errors.New("SQlite aggregator doesn't have a Step() function")
831: 	}
832: 	step := stepFn.Type
833: 	if step.NumOut() != 0 && step.NumOut() != 1 {
834: 		return errors.New("SQlite aggregator Step() function must return 0 or 1 values")
835: 	}
836: 	if step.NumOut() == 1 && !step.Out(0).Implements(reflect.TypeOf((*error)(nil)).Elem()) {
837: 		return errors.New("type of SQlite aggregator Step() return value must be error")
838: 	}
839: 
840: 	stepNArgs := step.NumIn()
841: 	start := 0
842: 	if agg.Kind() == reflect.Ptr {
843: 		// Skip over the method receiver
844: 		stepNArgs--
845: 		start++
846: 	}
847: 	if step.IsVariadic() {
848: 		stepNArgs--
849: 	}
850: 	for i := start; i < start+stepNArgs; i++ {
851: 		conv, err := callbackArg(step.In(i))
852: 		if err != nil {
853: 			return err
854: 		}
855: 		ai.stepArgConverters = append(ai.stepArgConverters, conv)
856: 	}
857: 	if step.IsVariadic() {
858: 		conv, err := callbackArg(step.In(start + stepNArgs).Elem())
859: 		if err != nil {
860: 			return err
861: 		}
862: 		ai.stepVariadicConverter = conv
863: 		// Pass -1 to sqlite so that it allows any number of
864: 		// arguments. The call helper verifies that the minimum number
865: 		// of arguments is present for variadic functions.
866: 		stepNArgs = -1
867: 	}
868: 
869: 	doneFn, found := agg.MethodByName("Done")
870: 	if !found {
871: 		return errors.New("SQlite aggregator doesn't have a Done() function")
872: 	}
873: 	done := doneFn.Type
874: 	doneNArgs := done.NumIn()
875: 	if agg.Kind() == reflect.Ptr {
876: 		// Skip over the method receiver
877: 		doneNArgs--
878: 	}
879: 	if doneNArgs != 0 {
880: 		return errors.New("SQlite aggregator Done() function must have no arguments")
881: 	}
882: 	if done.NumOut() != 1 && done.NumOut() != 2 {
883: 		return errors.New("SQLite aggregator Done() function must return 1 or 2 values")
884: 	}
885: 	if done.NumOut() == 2 && !done.Out(1).Implements(reflect.TypeOf((*error)(nil)).Elem()) {
886: 		return errors.New("second return value of SQLite aggregator Done() function must be error")
887: 	}
888: 
889: 	conv, err := callbackRet(done.Out(0))
890: 	if err != nil {
891: 		return err
892: 	}
893: 	ai.doneRetConverter = conv
894: 	ai.active = make(map[int64]reflect.Value)
895: 	ai.next = 1
896: 
897: 	// ai must outlast the database connection, or we'll have dangling pointers.
898: 	c.aggregators = append(c.aggregators, &ai)
899: 
900: 	cname := C.CString(name)
901: 	defer C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cname))
902: 	opts := C.SQLITE_UTF8
903: 	if pure {
904: 		opts |= C.SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC
905: 	}
906: 	rv := sqlite3CreateFunction(c.db, cname, C.int(stepNArgs), C.int(opts), newHandle(c, &ai), nil, C.stepTrampoline, C.doneTrampoline)
907: 	if rv != C.SQLITE_OK {
908: 		return c.lastError()
909: 	}
910: 	return nil
911: }

924: // Note: may be called with db == nil
925: func lastError(db *C.sqlite3) error {
926: 	rv := C.sqlite3_errcode(db) // returns SQLITE_NOMEM if db == nil
927: 	if rv == C.SQLITE_OK {
928: 		return nil
929: 	}
930: 	extrv := C.sqlite3_extended_errcode(db)    // returns SQLITE_NOMEM if db == nil
931: 	errStr := C.GoString(C.sqlite3_errmsg(db)) // returns "out of memory" if db == nil
932: 
933: 	// https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/system_errno.html
934: 	// sqlite3_system_errno is only meaningful if the error code was SQLITE_CANTOPEN,
935: 	// or it was SQLITE_IOERR and the extended code was not SQLITE_IOERR_NOMEM
936: 	var systemErrno syscall.Errno
937: 	if rv == C.SQLITE_CANTOPEN || (rv == C.SQLITE_IOERR && extrv != C.SQLITE_IOERR_NOMEM) {
938: 		systemErrno = syscall.Errno(C.sqlite3_system_errno(db))
939: 	}
940: 
941: 	return Error{
942: 		Code:         ErrNo(rv),
943: 		ExtendedCode: ErrNoExtended(extrv),
944: 		SystemErrno:  systemErrno,
945: 		err:          errStr,
946: 	}
947: }

954: func (c *SQLiteConn) exec(ctx context.Context, query string, args []driver.NamedValue) (driver.Result, error) {
955: 	// Fast path: no args, no context cancellation → single CGO call per statement
956: 	if len(args) == 0 && ctx.Done() == nil {
957: 		return c.execNoArgs(query)
958: 	}
959: 
960: 	start := 0
961: 	for {
962: 		s, err := c.prepareWithCache(ctx, query)
963: 		if err != nil {
964: 			return nil, err
965: 		}
966: 		var res driver.Result
967: 		if s.(*SQLiteStmt).s != nil {
968: 			na := s.NumInput()
969: 			if len(args)-start < na {
970: 				s.Close()
971: 				return nil, fmt.Errorf("not enough args to execute query: want %d got %d", na, len(args))
972: 			}
973: 			stmtArgs := stmtArgs(args, start, na)
974: 			res, err = s.(*SQLiteStmt).exec(ctx, stmtArgs)
975: 			if err != nil && err != driver.ErrSkip {
976: 				s.Close()
977: 				return nil, err
978: 			}
979: 			start += na
980: 		}
981: 		tail := s.(*SQLiteStmt).t
982: 		s.Close()
983: 		if tail == "" {
984: 			if res == nil {
985: 				// https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/963
986: 				res = &SQLiteResult{0, 0}
987: 			}
988: 			return res, nil
989: 		}
990: 		query = tail
991: 	}
992: }

994: // execNoArgs executes a query with no parameters in a single CGO call per statement.
995: func (c *SQLiteConn) execNoArgs(query string) (driver.Result, error) {
996: 	var res *SQLiteResult
997: 	for len(query) > 0 {
998: 		var rowid, changes C.longlong
999: 		var tail *C.char
1000: 		pquery := C.CString(query)
1001: 		rv := C._sqlite3_exec_no_args(c.db, pquery, C.int(len(query)), &rowid, &changes, &tail)
1002: 		if tail != nil && *tail != '\000' {
1003: 			query = strings.TrimSpace(C.GoString(tail))
1004: 		} else {
1005: 			query = ""
1006: 		}
1007: 		C.free(unsafe.Pointer(pquery))
1008: 		if rv != C.SQLITE_ROW && rv != C.SQLITE_OK && rv != C.SQLITE_DONE {
1009: 			return nil, c.lastError()
1010: 		}
1011: 		res = &SQLiteResult{id: int64(rowid), changes: int64(changes)}
1012: 	}
1013: 	if res == nil {
1014: 		res = &SQLiteResult{0, 0}
1015: 	}
1016: 	return res, nil
1017: }

1024: func (c *SQLiteConn) query(ctx context.Context, query string, args []driver.NamedValue) (driver.Rows, error) {
1025: 	start := 0
1026: 	for {
1027: 		s, err := c.prepareWithCache(ctx, query)
1028: 		if err != nil {
1029: 			return nil, err
1030: 		}
1031: 		ss := s.(*SQLiteStmt)
1032: 		ss.cls = true
1033: 		// sqlite3_prepare_v2 returns SQLITE_OK with a NULL statement handle
1034: 		// when the input is empty or contains only whitespace/comments.
1035: 		if ss.s == nil {
1036: 			tail := ss.t
1037: 			ss.Close()
1038: 			if tail == "" {
1039: 				return &SQLiteRows{cls: true, ctx: ctx}, nil
1040: 			}
1041: 			query = tail
1042: 			continue
1043: 		}
1044: 		na := s.NumInput()
1045: 		if len(args)-start < na {
1046: 			ss.Close()
1047: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("not enough args to execute query: want %d got %d", na, len(args)-start)
1048: 		}
1049: 		stmtArgs := stmtArgs(args, start, na)
1050: 		rows, err := ss.query(ctx, stmtArgs)
1051: 		if err != nil && err != driver.ErrSkip {
1052: 			ss.Close()
1053: 			return rows, err
1054: 		}
1055: 		start += na
1056: 		tail := ss.t
1057: 		if tail == "" {
1058: 			return rows, nil
1059: 		}
1060: 		rows.Close()
1061: 		ss.Close()
1062: 		query = tail
1063: 	}
1064: }

1078: // Open database and return a new connection.
1079: //
1080: // A pragma can take either zero or one argument.
1081: // The argument is may be either in parentheses or it may be separated from
1082: // the pragma name by an equal sign. The two syntaxes yield identical results.
1083: // In many pragmas, the argument is a boolean. The boolean can be one of:
1084: //
1085: //	1 yes true on
1086: //	0 no false off
1087: //
1088: // You can specify a DSN string using a URI as the filename.
1089: //
1090: //	test.db
1091: //	file:test.db?cache=shared&mode=memory
1092: //	:memory:
1093: //	file::memory:
1094: //
1095: //	mode
1096: //	  Access mode of the database.
1097: //	  https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/open.html
1098: //	  Values:
1099: //	   - ro
1100: //	   - rw
1101: //	   - rwc
1102: //	   - memory
1103: //
1104: //	cache
1105: //	  SQLite Shared-Cache Mode
1106: //	  https://www.sqlite.org/sharedcache.html
1107: //	  Values:
1108: //	    - shared
1109: //	    - private
1110: //
1111: //	immutable=Boolean
1112: //	  The immutable parameter is a boolean query parameter that indicates
1113: //	  that the database file is stored on read-only media. When immutable is set,
1114: //	  SQLite assumes that the database file cannot be changed,
1115: //	  even by a process with higher privilege,
1116: //	  and so the database is opened read-only and all locking and change detection is disabled.
1117: //	  Caution: Setting the immutable property on a database file that
1118: //	  does in fact change can result in incorrect query results and/or SQLITE_CORRUPT errors.
1119: //
1120: // go-sqlite3 adds the following query parameters to those used by SQLite:
1121: //
1122: //	_loc=XXX
1123: //	  Specify location of time format. It's possible to specify "auto".
1124: //
1125: //	_mutex=XXX
1126: //	  Specify mutex mode. XXX can be "no", "full".
1127: //
1128: //	_txlock=XXX
1129: //	  Specify locking behavior for transactions.  XXX can be "immediate",
1130: //	  "deferred", "exclusive".
1131: //
1132: //	_auto_vacuum=X | _vacuum=X
1133: //	  0 | none - Auto Vacuum disabled
1134: //	  1 | full - Auto Vacuum FULL
1135: //	  2 | incremental - Auto Vacuum Incremental
1136: //
1137: //	_busy_timeout=XXX"| _timeout=XXX
1138: //	  Specify value for sqlite3_busy_timeout.
1139: //
1140: //	_case_sensitive_like=Boolean | _cslike=Boolean
1141: //	  https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_case_sensitive_like
1142: //	  Default or disabled the LIKE operation is case-insensitive.
1143: //	  When enabling this options behaviour of LIKE will become case-sensitive.
1144: //
1145: //	_defer_foreign_keys=Boolean | _defer_fk=Boolean
1146: //	  Defer Foreign Keys until outermost transaction is committed.
1147: //
1148: //	_foreign_keys=Boolean | _fk=Boolean

type functionInfo struct {
	f                 reflect.Value
	argConverters     []callbackArgConverter
	variadicConverter callbackArgConverter
	retConverter      callbackRetConverter
}

func (fi *functionInfo) Call(ctx *C.sqlite3_context, argv []*C.sqlite3_value) {
	args, err := callbackConvertArgs(argv, fi.argConverters, fi.variadicConverter)
	if err != nil {
		callbackError(ctx, err)
		return
	}

	ret := fi.f.Call(args)

	if len(ret) == 2 && ret[1].Interface() != nil {
		callbackError(ctx, ret[1].Interface().(error))
		return
	}

	err = fi.retConverter(ctx, ret[0])
	if err != nil {
		callbackError(ctx, err)
		return
	}
}

type aggInfo struct {
	constructor reflect.Value

	// Active aggregator objects for aggregations in flight. The
	// aggregators are indexed by a counter stored in the aggregation
	// user data space provided by sqlite.
	active map[int64]reflect.Value
	next   int64

	stepArgConverters     []callbackArgConverter
	stepVariadicConverter callbackArgConverter

	doneRetConverter callbackRetConverter
}

func (ai *aggInfo) agg(ctx *C.sqlite3_context) (int64, reflect.Value, error) {
	aggIdx := (*int64)(C.sqlite3_aggregate_context(ctx, C.int(8)))
	if *aggIdx == 0 {
		*aggIdx = ai.next
		ret := ai.constructor.Call(nil)
		if len(ret) == 2 && ret[1].Interface() != nil {
			return 0, reflect.Value{}, ret[1].Interface().(error)
		}
		if ret[0].IsNil() {
			return 0, reflect.Value{}, errors.New("aggregator constructor returned nil state")
		}
		ai.next++
		ai.active[*aggIdx] = ret[0]
	}
	return *aggIdx, ai.active[*aggIdx], nil
}

func (ai *aggInfo) Step(ctx *C.sqlite3_context, argv []*C.sqlite3_value) {
	_, agg, err := ai.agg(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		callbackError(ctx, err)
		return
	}

	args, err := callbackConvertArgs(argv, ai.stepArgConverters, ai.stepVariadicConverter)
	if err != nil {
		callbackError(ctx, err)
		return
	}

	ret := agg.MethodByName("Step").Call(args)
	if len(ret) == 1 && ret[0].Interface() != nil {
		callbackError(ctx, ret[0].Interface().(error))
		return
	}
}

func (ai *aggInfo) Done(ctx *C.sqlite3_context) {
	idx, agg, err := ai.agg(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		callbackError(ctx, err)
		return
	}
	defer func() { delete(ai.active, idx) }()

	ret := agg.MethodByName("Done").Call(nil)
	if len(ret) == 2 && ret[1].Interface() != nil {
		callbackError(ctx, ret[1].Interface().(error))
		return
	}

	err = ai.doneRetConverter(ctx, ret[0])
	if err != nil {
		callbackError(ctx, err)
		return
	}
}

// Commit transaction.
func (tx *SQLiteTx) Commit() error {
	_, err := tx.c.exec(context.Background(), "COMMIT", nil)
	if err != nil {
		// sqlite3 may leave the transaction open in this scenario.
		// However, database/sql considers the transaction complete once we
		// return from Commit() - we must clean up to honour its semantics.
		// We don't know if the ROLLBACK is strictly necessary, but according
		// to sqlite's docs, there is no harm in calling ROLLBACK unnecessarily.
		tx.c.exec(context.Background(), "ROLLBACK", nil)
	}
	return err
}

// Rollback transaction.
func (tx *SQLiteTx) Rollback() error {
	_, err := tx.c.exec(context.Background(), "ROLLBACK", nil)
	return err
}

// RegisterCollation makes a Go function available as a collation.
//
// cmp receives two UTF-8 strings, a and b. The result should be 0 if
// a==b, -1 if a < b, and +1 if a > b.
//
// cmp must always return the same result given the same
// inputs. Additionally, it must have the following properties for all
// strings A, B and C: if A==B then B==A; if A==B and B==C then A==C;
// if A<B then B>A; if A<B and B<C then A<C.
//
// If cmp does not obey these constraints, sqlite3's behavior is
// undefined when the collation is used.
func (c *SQLiteConn) RegisterCollation(name string, cmp func(string, string) int) error {
	handle := newHandle(c, cmp)
	cname := C.CString(name)
	defer C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cname))
	rv := C.sqlite3_create_collation(c.db, cname, C.SQLITE_UTF8, handle, (*[0]byte)(unsafe.Pointer(C.compareTrampoline)))
	if rv != C.SQLITE_OK {
		return c.lastError()
	}
	return nil
}

// RegisterCommitHook sets the commit hook for a connection.
//
// If the callback returns non-zero the transaction will become a rollback.
//
// If there is an existing commit hook for this connection, it will be
// removed. If callback is nil the existing hook (if any) will be removed
// without creating a new one.
func (c *SQLiteConn) RegisterCommitHook(callback func() int) {
	if callback == nil {
		C.sqlite3_commit_hook(c.db, nil, nil)
	} else {
		C.sqlite3_commit_hook(c.db, (*[0]byte)(C.commitHookTrampoline), newHandle(c, callback))
	}
}

// RegisterRollbackHook sets the rollback hook for a connection.
//
// If there is an existing rollback hook for this connection, it will be
// removed. If callback is nil the existing hook (if any) will be removed
// without creating a new one.
func (c *SQLiteConn) RegisterRollbackHook(callback func()) {
	if callback == nil {
		C.sqlite3_rollback_hook(c.db, nil, nil)
	} else {
		C.sqlite3_rollback_hook(c.db, (*[0]byte)(C.rollbackHookTrampoline), newHandle(c, callback))
	}
}

// RegisterUpdateHook sets the update hook for a connection.
//
// The parameters to the callback are the operation (one of the constants
// SQLITE_INSERT, SQLITE_DELETE, or SQLITE_UPDATE), the database name, the
// table name, and the rowid.
//
// If there is an existing update hook for this connection, it will be
// removed. If callback is nil the existing hook (if any) will be removed
// without creating a new one.
func (c *SQLiteConn) RegisterUpdateHook(callback func(int, string, string, int64)) {
	if callback == nil {
		C.sqlite3_update_hook(c.db, nil, nil)

	}
}

// RegisterAuthorizer sets the authorizer for connection.
//
// The parameters to the callback are the operation (one of the constants
// SQLITE_INSERT, SQLITE_DELETE, or SQLITE_UPDATE), and 1 to 3 arguments,
// depending on operation. More details see:
// https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/c_alter_table.html
func (c *SQLiteConn) RegisterAuthorizer(callback func(int, string, string, string) int) {
	if callback == nil {
		C.sqlite3_set_authorizer(c.db, nil, nil)
	} else {
